title: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Ltd - 544286 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Niva Bupa H1 FY27 combined ratio improved 365bps to 99.5%, with GWP up 26% to INR5,004 crores ex-1/n and PAT at INR273 crores.
summary.overview: Management reported a strong H1 FY27, with GWP ex-1/n up 26% to INR5,004 crores and retail GWP ex-1/n up 37% to about INR3,800 crores. Combined insurance service ratio improved 365bps to 99.5%, driven by a 287bps lower claims ratio and a 78bps lower expense ratio. Profit after tax on Ind AS basis rose to INR273 crores from INR132 crores. Solvency fell to 2.03x (regulatory minimum 1.50x), which drew the most scrutiny, along with questions on claims settlement perception and draft distribution commission norms.

financial_highlights.change: up from ~75% at end of Q1
from 38% in H1 FY26; allowable 36.1% incl. additional allowances
declining over last 7-8 quarters; regulatory minimum 1.50x

segments.name: Retail health
segments.commentary: Retail loss ratio 67.4% in H1, improved 77bps; management said growth in fresh business has been high-LTV and higher sum insured mix. October growth still in the 30s per management.

segments.name: Group / B2B and affinity
segments.commentary: Management said group B2B was flat to degrowing on pricing discipline; the group loss ratio improvement was attributed to mix shift toward SME and affinity/attachment, not to better underlying loss ratios.

segments.name: Renewal vs new business
segments.commentary: Renewal book claims ratio held around 75%; combined ratio is about 97-98% for renewal vs 102-103% for new business, per management.

guidance_outlook: Management expects CISR of 98-99% to continue going forward, balancing claims and expense of management including acquisition cost.
Investment yield of 7.4-7.5% seen as sustainable in the foreseeable future, as fresh investments are at higher yields; equity/ETF book at about 5.5%.
Target mid-to-high teens ROE; any excess to be passed on to customers once rules are in place.
No equity raise expected; board approval exists to raise up to INR500 crores of debt if needed.
Acquisition ratio currently about 29%; would be about 21% under proposed regulator commission rates, but final impact too early to quantify due to mix effects.
Retail loss ratio to be managed toward a combined ratio via steady portfolio management, with no one-offs expected.
capex_capacity: PPN network: present in 49 cities and 1,132 hospitals; 22% of cashless claims in those hospitals going to PPN setups, which are 15-20% cheaper than tertiary/quaternary care on a like-to-like basis.
Common empanelment MOUs signed with more than 5,000 hospitals; 18 standard treatment workflows going live out of 154 (ICMR defined), on top of 8 infectious disease admission criteria.
Industry awareness campaign of about INR150 crores over 3 years, per management.
demand_pricing: Retail growth driven by GST tailwind and the 1/n industry impact; management cited price elasticity seen after GST.
Fresh business ticket sizes and higher sum insured mix rising; ReAssure 3.0 product cited as improving fresh claims ratios.
Attachment (loan-linked) business volume expected to stay steady; value may fall under lower commissions, per management.
Management expects Policybazaar-led business to grow at market rate despite commission changes; working with all distribution partners on new models.
Management said retention rates have been improving and NPS on claims rising, with Gen AI helping claims decisions.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the loss ratio improvement is from weaker monsoon/seasonal infections vs wellness and underwriting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said infection levels were in line with the 3-year average, slightly below last year. Most of the improvement was attributed to writing high-LTV business; the split between factors could not be quantified, and wellness impact is hard to isolate.

qa_highlights.question: Is the claims ratio improvement from fresh growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewal claims ratio is steady around 75%. Fresh business claims ratio improved, with a higher sum insured mix and ReAssure 3.0; new-book age profile is similar to earlier years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is retail claims settlement perceived low by brokers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited public settlement and complaint data, retention rates, and claims NPS as evidence. It said retail rejections are structurally higher due to waiting periods and exclusions, while corporate settlement is 98-99%. Per-rupee settlement data is not public.

qa_highlights.question: Why has solvency declined and how will it be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Solvency is still on Indian GAAP and based on premium-linked ASM; H1 has seasonal low solvency and profits come in H2. Management said it is comfortable at 2.03x with no equity raise needed.

qa_highlights.question: How will draft commission norms affect premiums and solvency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will pass on excess returns to customers but considers the claims-based solvency impact too premature to quantify until the RBC/QIS draft is released.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the group loss ratio change, and how are investments classified?
qa_highlights.answer: Group loss ratio improvement was attributed to mix (SME, affinity) rather than underlying improvement. Government and corporate bonds are at FVOCI; ETFs, AIFs and liquid funds are at FVTPL; a small FD book is at book value.

risks_watch: Draft distribution commission norms could cut acquisition costs (29% to about 21%) but may reduce attachment and Policybazaar volumes; impact on premiums and solvency is unclear.
Solvency has declined over the last 7-8 quarters to 2.03x; the ASM is premium-based and could come under pressure if claims-based RSM or RBC rules apply.
Perception risk around claims payments raised by brokers; management pointed to public data but the issue could affect word-of-mouth growth.
Sustainability of the low H1 loss ratio given that infection levels may normalise and the business mix is shifting.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating metrics such as the combined ratio, claims settlement and NPS, but defensive when questioned on claims perception and vague on the impact of draft commission norms ("too early to say"). Management was firm that the loss ratio gains are structural and not one-off.
key_quotes: I would say no one-offs, but steady, I would say, steady portfolio management is what you should continue to expect from us.
So where it will end, we will wait for some more clarity from the regulator side and then we'll be able to share with you.

growth.why: Management guided to CISR of 98-99% and mid-to-high teens ROE but gave no revenue growth number; H1 GWP ex-1/n grew 26% (retail 37%) on GST tailwind and 1/n industry impact, with October retail growth in the 30s, while group B2B was flat to degrowing and no capacity or order book was cited as backing.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: CISR guided at 98-99% going forward vs 99.5% H1 (down from 102.2% prior year), but acquisition ratio of ~29% could fall to ~21% under proposed commission norms, though final impact is unquantified.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new capacity, branches or plants discussed; PPN network (1,132 hospitals, 22% of cashless claims) is a network expansion, not capacity build-out.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 GWP ex-1/n up 26% to INR5,004 crores and retail up 37% to ~INR3,800 crores, with October retail growth still in the 30s, though group B2B was flat to degrowing and draft commission norms could weigh on Policybazaar and attachment volumes.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the insurer is asset-light and the only capital item noted is debt headroom of up to INR500 crores, with no equity raise expected.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held CISR at 98-99% and mid-to-high teens ROE, and its H1 combined ratio of 99.5% is already at the top end of that band, with no revenue guidance given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management said the H1 loss ratio may not hold as infection levels normalise, group B2B is flat to degrowing, and solvency is at 2.03x against a 1.50x minimum, with the commission-norm impact unquantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product launch was announced; ReAssure 3.0 is already live and is cited for improving fresh claims ratios, and 18 of 154 standard treatment workflows are going live.

rows.label: Draft commission norms and RBC/QIS rules
rows.why: Acquisition ratio of ~29% could fall to ~21% under proposed rates, but attachment and Policybazaar volumes may fall and solvency impact awaits the RBC/QIS draft.

rows.label: Solvency pressure at 2.03x
rows.why: Solvency has declined for 7-8 quarters to 2.03x against a 1.50x minimum, and H1 is seasonally low, with H2 profits expected to rebuild it; no equity raise is planned.

rows.label: Group B2B flat to degrowing
rows.why: Management said group B2B was flat to degrowing on pricing discipline, and the group loss ratio gain came from mix shift rather than underlying improvement.

tone.note: Management was confident on the combined ratio, claims settlement and NPS and called the loss ratio gains structural, but was defensive on claims perception and vague on commission-norm impact; analysts pressed on solvency decline, claims settlement perception and draft commission norms.
